sections.markdown:
## C — The four document categories, identity and lawful status documents, Social Security proof, residency proof and affidavits, document acceptance rules, non-compliant credentials, teen crash risk factors, tips for teens and parents, off-road vehicle helmets, voter and Selective Service registration
Knowledge domain: the documents a first-time Indiana applicant must bring to get a learner's permit, driver's license or ID card, how the BMV judges those documents, what a non-compliant credential is, the main crash risks for teen drivers with the manual's tips for teens and parents, the helmet rule for young off-road vehicle riders, and the voter, Selective Service and registration renewal services offered alongside a credential.

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus 2 documents proving Indiana residency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-94 form showing the most recent admission or current status. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A02
A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-2, a 1099 or a pre-printed pay stub. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A02
An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-94 instead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A02
Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A02
A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within 60 days of applying. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A03
A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within one year of applying. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A03
An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A03
An applicant without 2 residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A03
For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least 18, signs the affidavit at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and 2 Indiana address documents. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A03
The BMV accepts only original documents or certified copies from the issuing agency and may refuse any document that looks fraudulent, unreliable, altered or expired. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A03
All documents must be in English or come with a verifiably accurate English translation, and your legal name and date of birth must match Social Security Administration records. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A04
A translation must be typed on the letterhead of a government entity, accredited school or translation agency, with a signed statement of accuracy and competence, and not done for a family member, friend or business associate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A04
A US citizen holding a valid non-compliant Indiana credential may choose another non-compliant credential, which is printed with NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES on the front. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A04
The leading contributor to teen crashes is errant, risky or distracted driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A04
The manual says the chance of a crash doubles with each passenger in a teen driver's vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A04
Most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen at intersections. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A04
Teen drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs are a small share but account for a much higher share of serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A04
Unless you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should not enter after it turns yellow. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A04
Talking on the phone or texting while driving is against the law, and even some over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A05
Parents are advised to practice driving with their teen during the learner's permit period and the first year of licensed driving, in varied conditions such as wet roads, snow, highways and night driving. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A05
Anyone under 18 operating or riding an off-road vehicle must wear a helmet meeting US Department of Transportation standards, and an owner may not knowingly let someone under 18 ride without one. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A05
Anyone eligible to vote may apply to register while completing a credential transaction at a branch, on myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A05
When authorized by a male under 26 getting a new or renewed license, the BMV sends his information to register him with the Selective Service, and failing to register is a felony. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A06
Vehicle registration can be renewed by phone, by mail, online at myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk, and for online, phone and mail renewals the plates and stickers arrive in about 21 days. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0078]

Misconceptions: a hospital souvenir birth certificate does not prove identity; an expired passport does not count; a post office box is not a residential address; renewing does not automatically bring a Real ID, the documents are needed for that; a teen with more passengers is not safer, the risk climbs with each one.
Mnemonics: one identity, one lawful status, one Social Security, two residency; bills and statements within sixty days, insurance within a year; the passenger count raises a teen's crash risk each time.
Glossary: Real ID-compliant credential means a credential meeting federal Real ID document rules; non-compliant credential means one marked not for Real ID purposes; I-94 means the federal arrival and status record; Indiana Residency Affidavit means a signed statement used when an applicant lacks residency documents; ORV means off-road vehicle.
Dynamic facts: acceptable document lists, the BMV phone line, REALID.IN.gov guidance, payment methods, mailing times and kiosk transactions can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.
